city_fields.supportSceneAlt: A doula walking alongside a pregnant Tempe mom on a Sonoran Desert path with Papago Park buttes in the distance
city_fields.culture: Tempe is the East Valley's central college town — home to Arizona State University's main campus, Tempe Town Lake, and roughly 185,000 residents. The city draws young, diverse families who want walkable neighborhoods and quick access to the whole Phoenix metro birth corridor. Tempe's birth community reflects that: families here can choose a high-volume hospital 10 minutes away in Mesa, a Dignity Health birth center in Chandler, or a fully out-of-hospital birth at a freestanding birth center in a historic 1920s house just off Mill Avenue — with a doula community comfortable supporting all three paths.
city_fields.medicaidNote: Yes — Arizona's AHCCCS (Medicaid) covers doula services. As of 2026, there are 27 AHCCCS-credentialed doulas throughout the state who can accept Medicaid as payment for doula services. Not all doulas are enrolled, so ask any Tempe doula you interview whether they are AHCCCS-approved and can bill Medicaid directly.
